---
title: Output & warnings
description: How unpacked output is laid out, named, and reported.
---

## Layout

`--unpack` writes one JavaScript file per recovered module into the output
directory. The directory must be new or empty unless you pass `--force`.

## Filenames

- Modules with real path evidence keep readable relative filenames. Evidence
  includes webpack string IDs, Browserify dependency maps, and original
  input paths.
- Everything else gets a stable generated name like `module-42.js`.
- Names that collide receive numeric suffixes.
- Emitted files always end in a JavaScript extension. A module recorded as
  `src/style.less` becomes `src/style.less.js`.
- For supported `@vercel/ncc` bundles, the bundle's inline startup code is
  written as `entry.js`.

## Warnings

Wakaru prints human-readable summaries by default. `--json` puts the same
information on stdout as structured output:

- Every warning carries an `is_error` field. `false` means non-fatal. An
  error-class warning fails the command, even when output files were
  written.
- In unpack mode, `total` counts modules and `failed` counts modules that
  errored during decompilation. Treat `failed > 0` as a failed run.

Check the command's exit status as well as the JSON. Files can be written
even when the command fails:

| Result | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Exit status 0 | Read the output and any non-fatal warnings |
| `failed > 0` | Some modules failed to decompile. Inspect the warnings before using the partial output |
| `failed: 0`, but a warning has `is_error: true` | The command still failed. Check the warning for the cause |

Add `--diagnostics` to check for conflicting declarations in the recovered code:

```bash
npx wakaru bundle.js --unpack --diagnostics --json -o out/
```

An error-class diagnostic can fail the command even when every module was
decompiled. See [CLI diagnostics](/reference/cli#diagnostics) for the checks.

## Validating an output tree

`debug validate` is an internal debugging tool, built for Wakaru's own
development. Use it when you suspect broken references or declarations in
the recovered modules:

```bash
npx wakaru debug validate out/
npx wakaru debug validate out/ --input bundle.js
```

It checks the emitted modules as one graph: dangling relative references,
broken imports and exports, duplicate declarations, writes to imported or
`const` bindings, and references to bindings left in another module.
With `--input`, it also compares undeclared names against the original bundle
to help distinguish missing bindings from globals the input already used.

The command exits nonzero when it finds anything. A finding is a reason to
inspect the code, not proof that Wakaru introduced a runtime failure. For
example, a write to a `const` can be unreachable or already present in the input.
`--input` compares undeclared names only, so it does not filter out those writes.

Validate normal output only. Raw output has no module-graph contract.
